title: Training for a (half-)marathon: Training volume and longest endurance run related to performance and running injuries
publisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: The study followed 556 half-marathon participants and 441 marathon participants with three questionnaires on running-related injuries, average weekly training volume and the longest endurance run.
In half-marathon runners, a weekly training volume above 32 km was associated with a faster finish time (beta -4.19 min, 95% CI -6.52 to -1.85).
In half-marathon runners, a longest endurance run above 21 km was associated with a faster finish time (beta -3.87 min, 95% CI -6.31 to -1.44).
A higher weekly volume (beta -1.81 percentage points) and a longer endurance run (beta -1.89 percentage points) were associated with a smaller percentage decline in pace during the half marathon.
In marathon runners, a weekly volume below 40 km was related to a slower finish time and a volume above 65 km to a faster finish time.
No associations between training volume or longest endurance run and running-related injuries were identified.
